title: Pipeline + Tensor Parallelism: Interconnect Edge-case Profiling
content:
Summary:

Short version: when running mixed pipeline+tensor-parallel setups for serving (sharded KV cache + streaming decode) we see periodic 5–20ms tail spikes on token-step latency that correlate strongly with cross-node NVLink/NIC saturation and an unexpected NCCL algo switch under specific sequence length / micro-batch alignment. This doc captures experiments, profiling commands, hypotheses, and immediate mitigations to reduce token jitter in production.

Context / why it matters:
- Customer-facing streaming scenarios need stable sub-50ms per-token latency. Spiky tails break interactive UX and increase P90/P99 costs.
- Recent Dedicated clusters have mixed interconnect topologies: NVLink rings inside node, NVSwitch on DGX-style, and variable PCIe to NIC paths for cross-node RDMA (RoCEv2).
- We added a KV cache sharding shim that pins cache shards to tensor-parallel ranks; that increased cross-rank communication frequency during cached-prefix hits.

Experiment summary (high-level):
- Models tested: Llama2-13B (f32 emulation), Llama2-70B distilled sharded fp16, custom 32B open model.
- Parallel config: TP=2, PP=2 (4 GPUs total per micro-batch pipeline), also TP=4 PP=1 for contrast.
- Cluster: 2 x 4-GPU nodes (each with NVLink pairs), connected with Mellanox NICs (100Gb RoCE) — topology asymmetric: node A GPUs [0,1] NVLink, [2,3] NVLink; cross-node comm routes through NIC for some rank pairs, through PCIe->NVLink->NVLink otherwise.
- Workloads: streaming decode with prefix cache hit rate 80%, dynamic sequence length 64–1024, micro-batch 1 (real-time tokens).

Measurement methodology:
- Tools: NVIDIA Nsight Systems (nsys), nvidia-smi dmon, nvtop, NCCL_TRACE/NCCL_DEBUG, ibstat/rdma counters, perf counters for CPU-side stalls.
- Env vars used: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL_ALGO=RING,TREE (explicit toggles), NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0/1, NCCL_IB_CUDA_SUPPORT=1, NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0.
- Captured: per-step token latency (client timestamps), per-GPU timeline from nsys, NCCL logs, and NIC tx/rx counters sampled at 100ms.

Key commands (notes to self):
- Run decode trace: 
  NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL NCCL_ALGO=ALL python -m serving.decode --model ll2-13b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 256 --interactive
- Start nsys capture on rank 0 container: 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=trace-rank0 --capture-range=process-only -- python ...
- RDMA counters: 
  ibv_devinfo && sudo perf record -a -e r8169:tx_packets -g -- sleep 10 (on the NIC host)

Observed behaviors (representative):
1) Deterministic 12–18ms spikes every ~40–80 tokens for certain sequence lengths (not tied to model compute peaks).
2) NCCL logs showed periodic fall-back from TREE to RING algo when message sizes crossed ~256KB boundary; fall-back correlated with increased latency.
3) NIC tx/rx counters show short bursts corresponding to spike times; on some rank pairs the path traversed additional PCIe hops (verified via topology mapping).
4) Nsight timelines showed the host thread waiting on a rendezvous (cudaEvent) after entering an allreduce, while other GPUs were idling for a few ms.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Algorithm switching in NCCL (TREE->RING) induced by message-size quantization leads to less efficient cross-node patterns for our topology and increases latency variance.
- H2: KV cache sharding introduces small frequent cross-rank sends that interact with pipeline micro-batch alignment and cause transient buffer contention on NIC, increasing tail latency.
- H3: PCIe/NIC path asymmetry (some ranks using PCIe->CPU->NIC) creates hot-paths; when the collective maps over that link, we see extra serialization.

Microbenchmarks executed:
- nccl-tests allReduce bandwidth sweep: vary message size 1KB -> 2MB, run on exact rank-to-rank mapping used by serving runtime. Observed local minima at sizes ~256KB and ~768KB (algorithm boundary effects).
- Host->GPU roundtrip microbenchmark to measure PCIe latency jitter under load (stress other processes) — showed jitter increases when NIC/CPU interrupt load is high.
- Simulated KV cache micro-sends: small payloads (512B–8KB) at 10–100Hz; measured cumulative NIC queue depth and observed drop in NIC scheduling fairness when message bursts aligned across ranks.

Representative numbers (for doc readers, noisy but useful):
- Baseline per-token mean: 28ms, p95: 42ms, p99: 76ms.
- With observed spikes: mean 29ms, p95 45ms, p99 112ms (spikes added >36ms tail events).
- nccl-tests (2 nodes, 4 ranks): at 200KB message size: throughput dropped 18% and latency increased by 9ms relative to 180KB.

Root cause analysis notes:
- NCCL has internal thresholds where it switches collective algorithms; those thresholds are sensitive to system topology (whether peers are GPUDirect-aware over IB vs CPU-relayed). In our mixed topology some collectives choose an algorithm with more synchronizations across hosts (TREE) vs a ring with long sequential hops. 
- When the runtime triggers KV-cache syncs at token boundaries, message sizes temporarily cross thresholds that cause NCCL to pick suboptimal code paths. The extra host synchronization causes the host-thread wait observed in nsys.
- On top of that, NIC scheduling is momentarily saturated because many small messages from multi-rank pipeline stages land near-simultaneously; RDMA NIC queues exhibit micro-inflation and we see a ~5–15ms dequeue delay.

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
1) NCCL_ALGO=RING (force ring) — removed the algorithm flip; reduced p99 by ~20% in many runs but not all (some topologies still had expensive PCIe hops).
2) Coarsen KV-cache messages: batch small cache invalidations into 8KB aggregated payloads (delay 1 token) — reduced NIC bursts; p99 improved ~30% but increased average CPU coalescing overhead by ~1–2ms.
3) Set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for a test (force CPU-relay) — result much worse, ruling out GPU IB paths as the only issue.
4) Topology-aware rank reordering (map tensor ranks to NVLink-adjacent GPUs to keep hot comms intra-node) — biggest single improvement when possible (~35% p99 drop) but constrained by PP layout.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should the runtime implement an adaptive coalescer that observes recent NCCL logs and forces message sizes away from algorithm thresholds?
- Is it feasible to pin KV shards to GPU subgroups so that most cache hits are intra-node? That would require rethinking memory footprint/replication.
- Can we add a lightweight RDMA queue-depth probe to detect imminent NIC saturation and momentarily smooth sends?

Proposed next steps (short-term roadmap):
- (P0) Implement a runtime flag: collective_size_pad_bytes (default 512B) that pads/coalesces collective payloads to avoid NNCL algorithm boundaries. Test across 3 cluster types. Owner: Trevor. ETA: 2 weeks.
- (P0) Add rank-placement heuristic in orchestrator for PP+TP runs: prefer NVLink adjacency for tensor pairs. Owner: Anika. ETA: 1 sprint.
- (P1) Prototype NIC queue probe (using ethtool/rdma counters) and integrate with KV-shim to delay bursts by up to 5ms. Risk: requires careful timeout tuning. Owner: Diego. ETA: 3 weeks.
- (P2) Upstream follow-up: open issue with NCCL team with reproducible microbenchmark and logs. Owner: Asha. ETA: next week.

Notes to product/console team (operational):
- Add quick metric: "collective_algo_switches" at serving route level (count when NCCL logs include an algo change). Can be inferred from worker logs. This will help tie customer incidents to flips.
- Consider exposing a per-deployment toggle to force NCCL_ALGO=RING for low-latency routes. Document trade-offs.

Misc (scratch / rough ideas):
- Could use a token-level jitter-aware scheduler that inserts micro-delays when many cache hits are detected concurrently across ranks. UX trade-off vs jitter smoothing.
- Investigate if model quantization changes (fp16/qat) significantly change message sizes and therefore algorithm selection.

Appendix: quick reproducible steps for devs
1) Checkout branch: rw-infra#perf/kvs-coalesce.
2) Start 2-node local testbed: orchestration yaml in examples/pp-tp-nvlink.yml (maps ranks to GPUs with known NVLink topology).
3) Run: 
   NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ALGO=ALL python experiments/streaming_load.py --model ll2-13b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 256 --tokens 1000 --trace out/trace.json
4) Collect NCCL log from containers and grep for "algorithm" lines; correlate with perf counters in /sys/class/net/mlx5_0/statistics/.
